data.name: Hameem
data.gender_notes: Hameem is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who protects and provides shelter and security. The name Hameem carries the meaning “Protector” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Hameem usually hope their child will grow to embody protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a boy who is a guardian and protector of his family and community
data.etymology: Hameem belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Protector.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hameem total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: حميم
in_arabic.meaning: خاص و منفرد، مختص و مخصوص، حميم يعني بسيار نزديک و صميمي
in_arabic.long_meaning: حميم از اسماء الله الحسنى است، يعني کسی که به همه چیز آگاه است و با همه چیز مرتبط است. اين نام در قرآن کريم نيز ذکر شده است. حميم به معناي نزديک و صميمي نيز آمده است.

in_urdu.name: حمیم
in_urdu.long_meaning: حمیم اردو میں ایک مقبول نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے اخذ کیا گیا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب خاص، منفرد یا مختص ہوتا ہے۔ یہ نام اللہ کے اسماء الحسنیٰ میں سے ایک ہے اور اس کا ذکر قرآن کریم میں بھی آیا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हमीम
in_hindi.long_meaning: हमीम एक लोकप्रिय इस्लामी नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से लिया गया है। इसका अर्थ विशेष, अनोखा या विशिष्ट होता है। यह नाम अल्लाह के सुंदर नामों में से एक है और इसका उल्लेख कुरआन में भी आया है।

in_pashto.name: حميم
in_pashto.long_meaning: حميم په پښتو کې يو مشهور نوم دی چې د عربي ژبې څخه اخستل شوی دی. دغه نوم خاص، انوکھی يا ځانګړي معنی لري. دا نوم د الله تعالی په ښو نومونو کې دی او په قرآن کریم کې يې ذکر شوی دی.

in_english.name: Hameem
in_english.long_meaning: Hameem is a significant name in Islamic culture, derived from Arabic roots. It means special, unique, or exclusive. This name is considered one of the beautiful names of Allah and is mentioned in the Quran. It signifies someone or something that is closely related or very intimate.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Hameem" holds a deep cultural significance in Muslim communities, as it represents the idea of being a protector and a provider. In many Muslim societies, the concept of "Hameem" is highly valued, and individuals who live up to this name are held in high regard. "Hameem" is also associated with the idea of being the head of the household and providing for one's family, which adds to its importance in traditional Muslim cultures.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Hameem" can be seen as a reminder of Allah's protective nature towards His creation. Muslims believe in Allah's promise to provide for His followers and protect them from harm, making the name a reflection of Allah's character and attributes. Furthermore, the name also emphasizes the spiritual importance of caring for the physical needs of oneself and their loved ones, as well as taking on the responsibility of providing emotional and spiritual support to those in need. Overall, the name "Hameem" can serve as a powerful reminder of both the cultural and spiritual importance of being a protector and a provider.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Protector" symbolizes One who protects and provides shelter and security. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Hameem serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of protector.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr (The Conquest of Egypt), c. 870 CE. In this historical account, Hameem ibn Thabit is mentioned as a distinguished companion of Caliph Al-Mu'izz li-Din Allah who led the army to conquer Egypt.
Ibn Khaldun, The Muqaddimah, c. 1377 CE. Hameem ibn 'Amr is cited as an example of a warrior-scholar who contributed significantly to the Islamic civilization during the Umayyad Caliphate.
historical_references.context: Umayyad Caliphate and the development of Islamic civilization
